description: Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης αποτελεί η προμήθεια των απαραίτητων ανταλλακτικών τακτικής συντήρησης 57 οχημάτων και η προμήθεια ελαστικών επισώτρων στο πλαίσιο των αναγκών της τακτικής συντήρησης του συνόλου των μηχανοκίνητων οχημάτων του Δήμου.

title: Greece – Harbour construction works – ΚΑΤΑΣΚΕΥΗ ΤΜΗΜΑΤΟΣ ΚΡΟΥΑΖΙΕΡΑΣ ΛΙΜΕΝΑ ΣΟΥΔΑΣ –ΕΚΣΚΑΦΕΣ ΠΥΘΜΕΝΑ
description: Η προτεινόμενη παρέμβαση αφορά την εκτέλεση βυθοκορήσεων στην ευρύτερη θαλάσσια περιοχή του λιμένα Σούδας και περιμετρικά της επέκτασης του νέου προβλήτα, με στόχο την εξασφάλιση ωφέλιμου βάθους έως 12,50 m. Οι εργασίες περιλαμβάνουν τη διαμόρφωση των απαιτούμενων λειτουργικών βαθών για την εξυπηρέτηση του νέου προβλήτα και του λιμένα, καθώς και τη δημιουργία κελιού περιορισμένης θαλάσσιας διάθεσης (Confined Aquatic Disposal – CAD) για τη διαχείριση μέρους των βυθοκορημάτων. Επίσης στην περιοχή έδρασης του νέου έργου επέκτασης του προβλήτα ‘ΑΔΡΙΑΣ’, το οποίο θα υλοποιηθεί με άλλη εργολαβία με τίτλο: «Κατασκευή Τμήματος Κρουαζιέρας λιμένα ΣούδαςΕπέκταση προβλήτα ‘ΑΔΡΙΑΣ’», θα γίνουν οι απαραίτητες βυθοκορήσεις για την εξυγίανση του πυθμένα με εκσκαφή και αφαίρεση του επιτόπου εδαφικού υλικού σε πάχος 5,0m περίπου, κλιμακωτά ακολουθώντας κατά το δυνατόν το ανάγλυφο του πυθμένα. Τα υλικά που θα προκύψουν από τις βυθοκορήσεις χαρακτηρίζονται ως μη επικίνδυνα και αδρανή και, σύμφωνα με τους εγκεκριμένους περιβαλλοντικούς όρους, τα αδρανή βυθοκορήματα θα διατεθούν σε εγκεκριμένη θαλάσσια περιοχή απόθεσης, ενώ τα μη επικίνδυνα βυθοκορήματα θα ενταφιαστούν εντός του κελιού CAD και θα καλυφθούν με στρώση αδρανών υλικών πάχους τουλάχιστον 3 m.

title: Netherlands – Repair and maintenance services of building installations – Onderhoud en Vervanging van Elektrotechnische- en Werktuigbouwkundige (Gebouwgebonden) Assets (E&W-Assets)
description: Afdeling Vastgoed Beheer van het Facilitair Bedrijf (FB) is voornemens een overeenkomst met één partij (of een combinatie van partijen) af te sluiten voor het uitvoeren van het werktuigbouwkundig en elektrotechnisch beheer en onderhoud van de gebouwgebonden E&W-assets binnen het vastgoed van GVB. Het onderhoud omvat periodiek, correctief en projectmatig onderhoud. De opdracht omvat het langjarig beheer en onderhoud van de gebouwgebonden elektrotechnische en werktuigbouwkundige (E&W-)assets binnen het vastgoed van GVB. De werkzaamheden omvatten periodiek, correctief en projectmatig onderhoud. De Raamovereenkomst heeft een totale maximale looptijd van acht (8) jaar, inclusief verlengingsopties. De geraamde waarde over de volledige looptijd bedraagt € 72.391.548,- exclusief btw en indexatie. De daadwerkelijke omvang van de werkzaamheden is mede afhankelijk van de ontwikkeling van het areaal, de onderhoudsbehoefte en de beschikbaarheid van investeringsbudgetten. GVB garandeert geen minimale afname.

title: Albania – Telecommunication consultancy services – Strengthening digital connectivity and the digital transformation of businesses and public services in Albania
description: The objective of this contract is to advance the implementation of Albania’s Digital Agenda in selected sectors by improving ICT infrastructure and aligning electronic communications policies with national and EU objectives. It will support the Albanian institutions, in particular the relevant Ministry and AKEP (hereinafter the beneficiaries) to increase their capabilities to promote trust in the global digital ecosystem by advancing inclusive and affordable connectivity so that all citizens can benefit from the digital economy and the future of Internet. In more details it will help prepare the documentations for conducting geographical survey and the methodology on very high capacity networks in the implementation of article 43 of the law no 54/2024 on electronic communication law in Albania in conformity with article 22 of EECC Directive and EU practice and drafting secondary legislation aligned with the EU regulation 2024/1309 for GIA, based on Very High-Capacity Networks (VHCN) with fibre optic and 5G. It will also perform the technical study for 5G use cases in smart communities based on EU best practices, design and implementation of a pilot project with 5G and awareness on gigabit infrastructure and 5G for relevant stakeholders.

title: Microscale thermophoresis device
description: Microscale thermophoresis device University of Oulu, Biocenter Oulu, seeks a spectral shift and microscale thermophoresis device to characterise qualitatively and determine quantitatively nanoparticle, including protein, interactions in the range of weak to tight binders in solution without immobilization (hereinafter referred to as the "device"). The device must enable the assessment of sample quality and aggregation and differentiating binding events from aggregation. The device will be used for analysis of interactions of fluorescence labelled proteins with small molecules and vesicles. The detection must be independent of the mass ratio of the binding partners. The device must enable fast screening of interactions as well as sensitive affinity measurement. The measurable dynamic range of dissociation constant must be at least in nM -mM range and binding affinity in at least nM -mM range. Low sample consumption (in order of 10 microlitre) and low nanomole of the labeled target is needed for the measurement. The device must enable detection of the interaction based on changes of emission spectrum of exited fluorophore under isothermal conditions and must be able to create a microscopic non-isothermal temperature field (temperature gradient) and determine nanoparticle including protein binding events based on the temperature related intensity change and fluorescence intensity change following thermophoresis under the thermal gradient. Intensity changes and/or spectrum shifts of the fluorescence probe versus ligand concentrations are measured and plotted to calculate the dissociation constant. The device must come with detailed documentation of all features. The device will be part of the Proteomics and protein analysis core facility infrastructure of Biocenter Oulu. The core facility has an open access policy, and the instrumentation and software must be easy to use and maintain. The device must include a user interface to control the operation. The device must be well suited to an academic multi-user environment. The contracting entity has a maximum sum of 189000 € (excluding value-added tax) available for the procurement and cannot accept tenders exceeding this amount. The procurement is partially funded by the European Regional Development Funds (ERDF), BioParts project (A81573).,

title: Technical Support Services for the FHWA Office of Safety and Operations Research & Development
description: The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) is conducting a market survey to identify potential sources for a series of anticipated contracts/task order awards capable of providing Technical Support Services for the FHWA Office of Safety and Operations Research & Development (HRSO) located at the Turner-Fairbank Highway Research Center (TFHRC) in McLean, VA. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information for planning purposes, regarding (1) the availability and capability of qualified sources to perform all or some of the work described below; and (2) the size classification of the available and capable sources relative to the North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition. The objectives of this requirement are to support and conduct research on why traffic crashes occur, to understand the factors that influence injury severity, and to identify the operational conditions that affect overall safety performance. The research will advance science? and data?driven approaches to developing countermeasures that address the underlying causes of crashes, including operational practices and emerging vehicle automation technologies that can enhance safety and reduce crash risk. The Contractor shall furnish non-personal technical support to continue and advance innovation to perform the activities described under this contract titled, �Technical Support Services for the FHWA Office of Safety and Operations Research & Development.� See Sources Sought Notice attached for more information.

title: Languages Testing for Interpreters
description: Services Requirement This requirement is for: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada Title: 20260726-IRB – Language Testing for Interpreters Description of the Requirement: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada has a requirement for service of testing components and test assessments for the recruitment of their interpreter contractors to Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB). Interpreter Services Contractors (ISCs) accredited by the IRB must successfully complete three (3) language tests with a minimum score of 70% to qualify for a contract: • Official Languages Test: Assesses the applicant’s ability to communicate in English or French. This is the first test administered, consisting of a short 15-minute written assessment designed to evaluate comprehension in one of the official languages. • Hearing Simulation (Oral) Test: Evaluates the applicant’s ability to perform consecutive interpretation between an official language and a target language, and vice versa. These tests are currently available in sixty (60) languages. However, there are only two versions of each language test, and the quality and consistency of the tests vary. • Sight Translation Test: Measures the applicant’s ability to translate short documents similar to those that may be presented in a hearing room from the language of interpretation to English or French. This is the final test administered. Level of Security Requirement: Resource(s) Minimum Security Level Required is Reliability Status. Associated Documents: Request for Proposal (RFP) 20260726-IRB. Proposed period of contract: The proposed period of contract shall be from September 30, 2026, to March 31, 2027. The resulting contract will include three (3) one-year optional periods. Estimated Level of Effort: The overall annual cumulative estimated level of effort of the contract(s) will be for 300 tests. Multiple contracts: Considering that contract(s) will be issue based on offerors qualified language(s), this solicitation could results on multiples contracts. Contracting Authority: Steve Dessureault Phone Number: 514-249-2780 Email address: steve.dessureault@irb-cisr.gc.ca Note: Please address all inquiry questions to the Contracting Authority by email only.

title: Sportplatz Murifeld, Umbau Natur- in Kunststoffrasenspielfeld, 425 Kunststoffrasensportplätze, 463 Belagsarbeiten Oberbau
description:
Der Eingriff beschränkt sich ausschliesslich auf das Spielfeld und den Randabschluss/Randplatte sowie die direkt angrenzenden Schächte. Die wertvollen Baumbestände dürfen nicht tangiert werden. An den Stirnseiten des Feldes wird bereits im Herbst 2026 bauseits ein Wurzelvorhang erstellt.

Aufgrund des Grundwasserschutzes ist zu verhindern, dass das anfallende Regenwasser

versickern kann. Dazu wird das Spielfeld mittels einer Bentonitmatte komplett abgedichtet. Auf der Abdichtung wird eine Retentionsanlage mit Kalkschotter erstellt, welche gleichzeitig als Koffer dient.

Für die Entwässrung des Kieskoffers werden Drainage-Saugleitungen auf die Sohle der Abdichtung verlegt (ohne Gefälle bzw. Grabenausbildung). Eine Sammelleitung mit Gefälle führt das Wasser aus dem geschlossenen System. Über einen Drosselschacht und einen Schlammsammler wird das Wasser anschliessend in die Zisterne eingespeist. Der Überlauf der Zisterne wird an die öffentliche Kanalisation angeschlossen und abgeführt. Grabarbeiten für die Elektroerschliessung Anzeigetafel und für die Installation der Bewässerungsanlage sind zu leisten.

Die erwähnten Arbeiten betreffend den BKP463 Oberbau.


Auf Produkte-/Marken-/Design- oder Typenbezeichnungen wird verzichtet. Sollten ausnahmsweise solche Bezeichnungen aufgeführt sein, sind gleichwertige Alternativen zugelassen. Die Gleichwertigkeit ist durch die Anbieter*in nachzuweisen.

title: Q702--Gainesville OPC IOTA
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Administration Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) August 13, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation Services in support of the Gainesville, FL OPC 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation (IOT&A) services for Gainesville, FL Outpatient Clinic (OPC). This requirement supports VHA's mission by providing contractor support services to help bring the hospital into full planned operations that will provide health care services to Veterans. This will be a firm-fixed-price contract with an estimated Period of Performance of 46-months. The North Florida/South Georgia Healthcare System has been approved for a major lease to create an expanded service opportunity for Veteran health care at Gainesville OPC Consolidation. This project proposes to lease a new outpatient clinic in Gainesville, FL. This project is approximately 188,418 net usable square foot (NUSF) in the vicinity of Gainesville, FL, including 1300 parking spaces. The clinic will expand on care currently provided at the existing contracted lease spaces and allow an expansion to the current footprint as well as added new for a decompression of the Malcom Randall VA Medical Center (VAMC) in Gainesville, FL. The lease would allow VA to consolidate outpatient services at one location for mental health, home based primary care, specialty care and ancillary diagnostics identified in the Strategic Capital Investment Planning (SCIP) process. The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project. The scope of services includes Comprehensive Project Management, Comprehensive Interior Design, FF&E, and Space Planning Support; CONOPS and Transitioning Planning; Acquisition Support Services to include package development, Activation, Delivery, Relocation and Installation, Training, and Turnover and Post Occupancy Support for the identified project. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 10 September 2026. Potential offerors are advised that there may be truncated response time on the solicitation that will follow this Pre-Solicitation notice. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 9 October 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. Any questions for this Pre-solicitation notice should be sent via e-mail to both Katherine.Johnson@va.gov and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov. No telephone requests/questions will be accepted. This Pre-Solicitation notice does not constitute a request for proposals. P.O.C: Katherine.Johnson@va.gov, Contract Specialist and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov, Contracting Officer

title: Passenger air terminal services at Naval Air Station Jacksonville, FL
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number N6883626QS049 is issued as a request for quote (RFQ), for Passenger air terminal services at Naval Air Station Jacksonville, FL. The services to be furnished under this contract provide Passenger Terminal Services in support of the Defense Transportation System (DTS) to include, but not limited to, all United States (U.S.) Government owned or operated aircraft; U.S. sponsored foreign Government or civil aircraft, Coalition Forces aircraft, North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), commercial contract aircraft, and commercial tendered aircraft. Services must facilitate on time aircraft departures and maintain the ability to provide sustained Passenger Terminal Services for a working Maximum on Ground (WMOG) capability of one wide-body aircraft or any combination of narrow-body aircraft which equate to one wide body aircraft. This acquisition is set aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Refer to attached RFQ for more information. title: Presolicitation for MSG cook services
description: Please note this solicitation is not ready to be issued as of this date. The U.S. Mission in Geneva will launch the solicitation on SAM.GOV when it is available. The Permanent Mission of the United States of America in Geneva, Switzerland, seeks qualified companies to provide food services. The Contractor shall perform food services work, five days a week from 11:00am to 5:00pm for the U.S. Mission Geneva Marine Security Guards. The Contractor shall furnish all managerial, administrative, and direct labor personnel that are necessary to accomplish the work in this contract. Contractor employee shall be on site. The anticipated performance period is for a base year with two one-year option periods, if exercised by the Government. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered. The U.S. Government intends to award a contract/purchase order to the responsible company submitting an acceptable offer at the lowest price. We intend to award a contract/purchase order based on initial quotations, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies in the competitive range if there is a need to do so. All contractors have to be registered in the SAM (System of Award Management) database prior to contract award pursuant to FAR provision 52.204-7. Therefore prospective offerors are encouraged to register prior to the submittal of quotations/proposals. This opportunity allows for electronic responses. Please submit your offer prior to the response date and time.

title: FCC TERRE HAUTE BREAD NOV26-SEP27
description: FCC TERRE HAUTE BREAD NOVEMBER 2026 THROUGH SEPTEMBER 2027 The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Complex located in Terre Haute, Indiana, is issuing this combined synopsis/solicitation for the requirements of: FCC Terre Haute BREAD FY27 prepared in accordance with FAR 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. This solicitation is a 100% Small Business set-aside. The NAICS code for this solicitation is 311812 with an employee size maximum of 1000. See the attached Statement of Work for specifications. The period of performance is November 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027. Deliveries Need to begin on November 1, 2026. Deliveries will be made to the Federal Correctional Complex 4700 Bureau Road South, Terre Haute, Indiana 47802. The Government reserves the right to make a single, or multiple awards based on best value. The Government will award to the responsible quoter(s) whose quote, conforming to the solicitation, is most advantageous to the Government based on best value. Best value will be determined by evaluating each quotation for one or more of the following: price, and past performance. THIS IS AN ALL OR NONE QUOTE; vendors should quote all items, to be considered most advantageous to the government based on best value. Quality, comparison with other offers, and administrative/shipping cost; with past performance that does not pose a risk to the government being the most important. Please input pricing that includes freight cost to our facility in your quotes. Your company can submit its quote on form 15B41826Q00000015; The quote will be evaluated per FAR 13.106-2 and the government may then issue a purchase order (contract) that must be signed by both parties to complete contractual agreement. Please fill out sections 17a., 30a., 30b. and 30c. along with each unity price and amount in the schedule of supplies / services. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 4.1102 requires all contractors seeking or currently doing business with the government to be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to award; information can be obtained at https://www.sam.gov/. All future information about this solicitation, including solicitation amendments, will also be distributed through this site. Interested parties are responsible for monitoring this site to ensure they have the most up-to-date information about this solicitation. The date for receipt of quotes is October 9, 2026, by 11:00 AM. The point of contact for all information regarding this solicitation is Richard Moothery, Contract Specialist. Completed AND signed quotes must be sent electronically to rmoothery@bop.gov. Payments will be made using Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) or via Government Purchase Card for awards of $15,000.00 or less. The only format in which questions will be answered is by e-mail (no phone calls please). Faith Based and Community Based Organizations have the right to submit quotes equally with other organizations for contracts for which they are eligible.

title: Large Area Display System (LADS)
description: Sources Sought Notice Number: H9224126S61892 The Technology Application Program Office (TAPO) is conducting market research to identify potential vendors capable of responding to the requirements described below. This is a Sources Sought Notice issued in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10 and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), nor does it oblige the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this request, so quotes will not be considered. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this synopsis or any follow-up information requests. Response is strictly voluntary; it is not mandatory to submit a response to this notice to participate in any formal RFP process that may take place in the future. However, it should be noted that information gathered through this notice may significantly influence the Government�s acquisition strategy. All interested parties will be required to respond separately to any solicitations posted as a result of this sources sought notice. Requirements: The Government seeks to identify potential sources with aircraft Large Area Display System (LADS) for military rotary wing Air Vehicle Systems (AVS) that are commercial products. These airborne avionics grade display system will serve as the primary human machine interface for pilotage and situational awareness tasks by the aircrew. Safety-critical video processing and control are expected to reside externally to the LADS. The Government is interested in a display subsystem capable of deterministic, bounded-latency presentation of video and symbology as an endpoint within an existing Cockpit Display System architecture. The system must be designed with a Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) to ensure interoperability, reusability, and future growth. Attributes of interest are Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP), environmental and electromagnetic susceptibility characteristics, and display characteristics. Further details are available to potential sources that the Joint Certification Program (JCP) have certified as eligible for access to unclassified, non-public military technical data and have a current JCP approved DD Form 2345, Military Critical Technical Data Agreement. Key Information: NAICS Code: 334511 (Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing). Interested sources may recommend other NAICS Codes for consideration. Small Business Size Standard: The small business size standard is 1,350 employees. PSC: 1680 - Miscellaneous aircraft accessories and components. Response Requested: Interested parties are invited to submit a capabilities statement (on company letterhead) demonstrating their qualifications, capabilities and experience in providing the requirement. Responses should be no longer than 10 pages and include the following: 1. Source Profile: A. Company Name and Address B. Affiliate Information (parent companies, joint ventures, potential teaming partners) C. Year Established & Number of Employees D. Two Points of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email) E. Unique Entity ID and CAGE Code (as registered in SAM: http://www.sam.gov/) F. Business Size & Designation (must correlate with SAM registration) 2. Technical Capability Describe the LADS offered relative to the requirement above, to include display size and resolution, luminance range and night vision imaging system compatibility, SWaP characteristics, video and symbology interfaces supported, and qualification and certification status. 3. Commercial Product Status A. Whether the LADS is of a type customarily used by non-governmental entities for other than governmental purposes, and whether it has been sold, leased, or licensed, or offered for sale, lease, or license, to the general public. B. FAA Technical Standard Order authorization, if any (TSO number and revision). C. Rotary wing installations under a Type Certificate or Supplemental Type Certificate, if any (TC/STC number, aircraft make and model, approximate units fielded). 4. Small Business Considerations A. Whether the respondent is the manufacturer of the LADS. If not, ability to comply with the nonmanufacturer rule. B. Ability to comply with the applicable limitation on subcontracting. 5. Administrative Current SPRS Basic Assessment score and date; current CMMC level and assessment type; foreign ownership, control, or influence status. Submission Details: Deadline: 09 October 2026, 11:00 A.M. Eastern Time Email: Responses are to be submitted via email to Dr. Petrina Stack petrina.v.stack.civ@socom.mil and Chiffon Bradshaw chiffon.m.bradshaw.civ@socom.mil Submit in PDF. Responses shall be UNCLASSIFIED. Mark any proprietary information accordingly. Important Note: Late responses will not be accepted. This is strictly market research; questions will not be entertained at this time. Submission of a response is voluntary and does not guarantee participation in any future RFP. All interested parties must respond separately to any future solicitations. Required Documentation: Interested sources must submit a Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Joint Certification Program (JCP) approved DD Form 2345, DD Form 2345 Military Critical Technical Data Agreement. Information on the JCP can be found at: https://www.dla.mil/Logistics-Operations/Services/JCP/ Controlled Document Access: To gain access to the documents in www.SAM.gov marked �Controlled�, requesters must first follow the below instructions and submit the approved DD 2345 to the POC�s indicated before access will be granted. Additionally, requesters must have an active www.SAM.gov CAGE code. Submit approved DD Form 2345 via email to the Contracting Officer at Petrina.v.stack.civ@socom.mil and the Contract Specialist at chiffon.m.bradshaw.civ@socom.mil. The request shall include the applicable posting number, and a copy of current, approved DD Form 2345. Any controlled data is subject to applicable data rights. The Government is not responsible for incomplete, misdirected, or untimely requests. Ensure your company is registered on the Joint Certification Program (JCP). If assistance is needed with JCP, the Help phone number is 1-877-352-2255. If you believe information within the National Industrial Security System (NISS) to be incorrect or non-current, contact your Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) Field Office to resolve. Once the approved DD2345 has been submitted, access should then be requested to Controlled documents provided on www.SAM.gov under this sources sought. If the DATA CUSTODIAN will be different for this particular request, please identify the individual in the email when sending the DD2345 that will submit the www.SAM.gov request for Controlled Document access. If assistance is needed with www.SAM.gov, the Help phone number is 1-866-606-8220.

title: Gestione globale del centro socio assistenziale San Michele di Entracque.
description: L’appalto ha per oggetto l’affidamento del servizio di gestione della struttura per anziani denominata “Centro socio assistenziale San Michele”, che costituisce la parte preponderante del contratto, oltre ai seguenti servizi integrativi: – fornitura del servizio infermieristico alla popolazione residente; – fornitura di bagni protetti agli anziani richiedenti; – fornitura di pasti da erogare a domicilio agli anziani richiedenti; – fornitura di pasti da erogare agli utenti della mensa scolastica comunale; – assistenza agli alunni trasportati sullo scuolabus comunale; – assistenza agli alunni frequentanti la mensa scolastica comunale; – pulizia locali indicati dal Comune, ambulatorio infermieristico; – servizi aggiuntivi a richiesta e discrezione del Comune. Il Centro socio assistenziale “San Michele” è una struttura di proprietà comunale, sita a Entracque in via Ospedale n. 72, nel centro del paese, ubicata in un edificio storico, un tempo utilizzato come Ospedale di carità e Ospizio. La sede è stata oggetto di ristrutturazione edilizia, di riqualificazione e di efficientamento energetico negli anni 2024-2026. La struttura, che permette un’ospitalità permanente, risulta in possesso delle autorizzazioni necessarie al funzionamento finalizzato alla “Progettazione ed erogazione di servizi socio-sanitari ed assistenziali rivolti ad anziani autosufficienti e non autosufficienti in regime di residenzialità”. Le caratteristiche della struttura e della gestione sono specificate nel progetto per l'affidamento della gestione globale del centro socio assistenziale "San Michele" approvato con deliberazione di Giunta del Comune di Entracque n. 52 del 24/06/2026; con deliberazione di Giunta del Comune di Entracque n. 64 del 26/08/2026 è stata invece approvata la versione aggiornata del quadro economico.

The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation or award a contract as a result of this notice. Responses to this notice are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this notice. Information received may be used by the Government to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether the anticipated requirement should be set aside for one or more small business programs. 2. AGENCY INFORMATION Department of the Interior National Park Service Contracting Operations (ConOps) East Point of Contact: Edward Dingle, Jr. Edward_dingle@ios.doi.gov 3. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Department of the Interior, National Park Service (NPS), is conducting market research to determine the availability and capability of qualified construction contractors to perform the Atrium Replacement at the Chickamauga Visitor Center, Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia, Project CHCH 315696. The contemplated project generally consists of replacement of the existing Visitor Center atrium, limited parking-lot modifications, reconfiguration of the north and south plazas, and associated fire-protection, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, communications, fire-alarm, architectural, structural, civil/site, and landscape improvements. The work is anticipated to be performed under a single prime construction contract and includes multiple interdependent construction disciplines requiring significant coordination by the prime contractor. Major elements of work include, but are not necessarily limited to: � Selective demolition and demolition of the existing Visitor Center atrium. � Construction of the replacement atrium, including structural, architectural, roofing, building-envelope, curtain-wall/glazing, entrance, and interior-finish work. � Civil, landscape, parking, pedestrian pathway, paving, grading, earthwork, stormwater, and related site improvements. � Fire-protection modifications, including dry-pipe sprinkler-system work. � Plumbing and facility drainage improvements. � HVAC/mechanical modifications, including associated piping, ductwork, equipment, controls, supports, vibration/seismic requirements, and testing and balancing. � Electrical modifications, including demolition, conductors, raceways, grounding, panelboards, wiring devices, lighting, and associated electrical distribution work. � Fire-alarm, communications, and related life-safety systems. � Temporary facilities and controls, environmental protection, construction waste management, testing, commissioning, project documentation, and closeout. The specifications separately identify contract line items covering site demolition, demolition of the existing Visitor Center atrium, civil and landscape improvements, construction of the new atrium, fire-sprinkler upgrades, plumbing/drainage upgrades, mechanical improvements, and electrical improvements. Areas outside the construction limits are expected to remain occupied by NPS personnel and accessible to park visitors. Construction activities must therefore be planned and coordinated to protect employees and the public, maintain access and required exits, and minimize disruption to park and Visitor Center operations. Temporary construction controls include fencing, barriers, and separation of construction activities from occupied/public areas. title: Market Survey - Microgrid - United States Army Garrison (USAG) Ansbach; Bavaria, Germany � Katterbach Kaserne
description: A market survey is being conducted to determine if there are a reasonable number of interested businesses for the below future project. If your firm is an Other than Small, Small Business, certified HUBZone, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business and you are interested in this project please respond appropriately. Project Location: United States Army Garrison (USAG) Ansbach; Bavaria, Germany � Katterbach Kaserne Project Description: This is a Design/Bid/Build project. The US Government intends to solicit to construction firms to perform military construction and other Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (SRM) projects in the country of Germany as described within this announcement for the state of Bavaria. Construct a fully functional, islandable, and black start capable microgrid. The microgrid will include solar photovoltaic (PV) power production to provide daily, on-site renewable energy generation to offset incoming power from the local utility. Additionally, this project will also include diesel fuel generators, a battery energy storage system (BESS), and a microgrid controller to control all energy generation assets and manage electrical loads. This microgrid system will connect and distribute power on a government owned electrical distribution system. This microgrid is to provide resilient power to facilities at Katterbach/Bismarck Kaserne. Contract duration is estimated at 743 calendar days. The estimated cost range is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. NAICS code is 237130. All interested Other than Small, Small Business, certified HUBZONE, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business contractors should respond to this survey via the form link or QR code provided on this posting by Friday, October 09, 2026 by 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Responses should include: Identification and verification of the company�s size status. Contractor�s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code(s). Identification of firm�s current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. Description of Experience � Provide descriptions on up to three (3) projects completed by you as the prime contractor or if the offeror is a Small Business, they can provide Past Performance of affiliates in accordance with DFARS 215.305(a)(2)(C). Submissions of Past Performance from affiliates shall include documentation of the affiliation to the offeror. To be relevant, the projects submitted should be greater than 95% construction complete or completed within the last five (5) years and are similar to this project in scope and complexity. Demonstrate experience including self-performing 15% of the construction. Provide documentation demonstrating experience for projects of similar type projects. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages and quality of performance. Projects similar in scope shall include construction of a microgrid demonstrating a sufficient combination of the following scope elements to substantiate the offeror's technical competency, based on the complexity, scale, and integration of the demonstrated elements: (1) Installation of diesel centralized generators to power multiple buildings and fuel tank farm system (2) Installation of necessary breakers and switchgears (3) Installation of photovoltaic systems (4) Installation of electrical and telecommunication duct bank (5) Installation of a BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) (6) Information and communication systems (7)Commissioning of microgrid systems Projects similar in size to this project include: Construction of microgrid systems that meet or exceed the following: (1) Construction and installation of diesel generators able to handle loads of .5 to 2.5MW (2) Construction and installation of a PV Array of power production of 500 kW to 1.5 MW (3) Construction and installation of a BESS of 2 MWh to 10 MWh Based on definitions above, for each project submitted include: (1) Current percentage of construction complete and the date when it was or will be completed. (2) Size of the project (3) Scope of the project (4) The dollar value of the construction contract (5) The percentage of work that was self-performed as project and/or construction management services or physical construction type work. (6) Whether the project was design build or design/bid/build (7) Identify the number of subcontractors by construction trade utilized for each project. 5. Small Businesses are reminded under RFO 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting; they must perform at least 15% of the cost of the contract, not including the cost of materials, with the firm�s own employees for general construction-type procurement. Include the percentage of work that will be self-performed on this project, and how it will be accomplished. Submission Requirement: The only authorized transmission method of responses is via filling out the survey form. No other transmission method will be accepted. Please limit your capability statement to the space provided within the form. The Market Survey Form can be accessed at https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/1uE70uE03H via the QR Code provided in SAM.gov. This is NOT a Request for Proposal and does not constitute any commitment by the Government. Responses to this sources sought notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. All interested sources must respond to future solicitation announcements separately for responses to this market survey. All proposed contractors are highly encouraged to review RFO Clause 52.232-33 Payments by Electronic Funds Transfer � System for Award Management, which indicates �All payments by the Government under this contract shall be made by electronic funds transfer (EFT).� Those not currently registered can obtain registration by going to the website http://www.SAM.gov. The process can usually be completed from 24 to 48 hours after submission. Contractors will need to obtain a Unique Entity Identifier (formerly DUNS number) for processing their registration. title: GLWACH Construct Hospital Parking and Renovate Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL)
description: W912DQ279A002 REQUEST FOR MARKET INFORMATION / NOTICE OF INDUSTRY WEBINAR FOR GENERAL LEONARD WOOD ARMY COMMUNITY HOSPTIAL (GLWACH) CONSTRUCT HOSPITAL PARKING AND RENOVATE OPTICAL FABRICATION LABORATORY (OFL) PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Kansas City District, is requesting market intelligence information to identify qualified industry partners capable of supporting a potential Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a for the stated General Leonard Wood Community Hospital (GLWACH) project at Fort Leonard Wood, MO. The Government is seeking industry feedback to better understand the commercial market interest, market capabilities, market capacity and innovative business practices that may inform the acquisition strategy and structure of the potential OT Agreement. This is not a Request for Qualifications. It does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award an agreement or reimburse respondents for costs associated with responding. Participation is voluntary. PROJECT OVERVIEW and REQUIREMENTS: Project Title: Hospital Parking Lot Construction and Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL) Renovation Location: Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri Agency: USACE, Kansas City District (NWK) NAICS Code: 236220-Commerical and Industrial Building Construction Planning and design activities are ongoing. The project�s phased funding profile is listed below: FY23: $31M (Expires September 30, 2027) FY29: $35M (Anticipated) The estimated magnitude for the entire overall effort is between $40 Million and $60M. The new General Leonard Wood Army Community Hospital requires the construction of new hospital parking lots, the renovation of an Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL), site work and infrastructure to support the newly constructed GLWACH. The parking lot construction includes site grading and drainage, vehicle circulation roads and parking, pedestrian sidewalks, landscaping (including the planting of trees), site lighting, wayfinding, and video surveillance. The contractor must always maintain 970 parking stalls during construction. The contractor must also ensure safe pedestrian access from the existing parking lots to the new hospital. A construction phasing plan and traffic management plan must be implemented to maintain a safe environment for hospital patrons and staff. The OFL renovation includes the demolition and replacement of the west wall at the current mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP) room, removing all equipment inside the MEP and capping all roof penetrations. After demolition the MEP space will remain and become additional storage space for the OFL contract. A new ADA (American with Disabilities Act) compliant entrance vestibule be provided on the west side of the building where the old connection to the hospital was. The OFL also includes the renovation of a medical supply warehouse. To meet life safety codes the optical fabrication lab (OFL) space on the lower level will receive a new egress corridor and lightning protection. The facility must remain fully operational during all deconstruction, demolition, and construction efforts. The former General Leonard Army Community Hospital and infrastructure must be decommissioned, dismantled, demolished, and removed prior to the construction of the new parking lot. This work included the decommissioning of a hospital and clinic, a central utility plant, abatement of hazardous materials and environmental liabilities. All existing paving, utilities, and other site appurtenances, including a helipad, must also be demolished and removed. Approximately 60,000 to 70,000 cubic yards of excavated soil will need to be cut and transported from an adjacent location to the project site for fill. POTENTIAL DELIVERY APPROACH: The Government is evaluating execution of this project using a Construction Manager At Risk (CMAR) Other Transaction Agreement authorized under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a with USACE as the Designer of Record (DOR). Using CMAR OT, the Government is particularly interested in commercial and collaborative practices to determine the following: Phasing and execution strategies to efficiently deliver the project Construction packaging and execution to optimize the given phased funding profile Early and continuous Government-industry collaboration; Collaborative design development and constructability; Contractor-Government open-book cost estimating and cost transparency; Collaborative project phasing and schedule certainty; Collaborative risk identification, mitigation and allocation; Innovation and alternative construction techniques; Overall cost, schedule, and mission outcomes. INDUSTRY INFORMATION REQUESTED: This request is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market intelligence regarding industry interest, capability and capacity, relevant experience using CMAR, open-book pricing, and potential commercial practices. The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding the use the same or similar collaborative commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of this project using CMAR under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Interested firms should complete and submit: The attached Market Intelligence Questionnaire and A summary of their interest and capabilities to perform all the work identified for this project. The summary interest and capabilities is not a formal Request for Qualifications, and the response should not exceed 10 pages in length. The summary should also include the following information: The Company information (name, address, contact information, business structure) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code and/or Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM.gov registration, if available. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Please submit the completed attached questionnaire and a summary of interest and capabilities via email to the individuals listed below no later than: 2:00 p.m. Central Time, 9 October 2026. Jeri L. Halterman at Jeri.l.halterman@usace.army.mil Courtesy copy: Dave Walsh at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. title: Tactical Data Link (TDL) Interoperability Software
description: Air Combat Command's (ACC) mission requires robust Tactical Datalink (TDL) interoperability to improve mission effectiveness for United States Air Force (USAF), Joint, and coalition forces. To support this mission, the Government requires a modern software solution that serves as a relational database and analysis toolset. This toolset is essential for the iSMART (interoperable Systems Management and Requirements Transformation) process and is used to populate, edit, analyze, and manage TDL message data, platform implementations, and interoperability evaluations. The Contractor shall provide an existing commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software solution, including all necessary licenses, updates, training, and technical support. The software shall provide a comprehensive toolset for managing TDL platform specifications, conducting interoperability analysis, and supporting mission planning across the TDL enterprise. The TDL software solution must meet all requirements as listed in the Attachment 1 - Performance Work Statement.

description: ***10 SEP 2026 - AMD 0001 issued*** The Army Contracting Command - Detroit Arsenal (ACC-DTA) is issuing this Request for Proposal (RFP) to establish a new five-year, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for the manufacture and delivery of four (4) variants of the S-280C/G Vehicle Mounted Shelter. This is a non-commercial requirement. Requirement: The S-280C/G is a lightweight, tactical military shelter designed to house and protect sensitive electronic equipment and personnel. Manufacturing shall be in strict accordance with the Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) and ASTM E1975-22. The scope includes First Article Testing (FAT), production, and delivery of all associated technical and logistics data. National Stock Numbers (NSNs): 5411-01-304-3069 (Shielded) and 5411-01-092-0892 (Unshielded). Set-Aside: This is a 100% Small Business Set-Aside. The applicable size standard for NAICS 332311 is 750 employees. Award Basis: The Government intends to award a single IDIQ contract to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This will be a tradeoff source selection conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15. Contract Value: The minimum guaranteed value for this contract is $100,000.00. The maximum estimated contract ceiling is $4,000,000.00. Technical Data Package (TDP): The TDP for this solicitation is Export-Controlled (Distribution Statement C). To gain access, interested parties must have a current and valid DD Form 2345, "Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement" certification on file with the U.S./Canada Joint Certification Office (JCO). The TDP can be accessed through the attachments section of this announcement on SAM.gov by certified offerors. Questions: All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing to the points of contact listed below no later than September 24, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. Points of Contact: Nicholas A. Lang, Contract Specialist, nicholas.a.lang.civ@army.mil Daniel J. Gibson, Contracting Officer, daniel.j.gibson43.civ@army.mil Disclaimer: Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for any amendments to this solicitation.

title: Pre-Solicitation Notice Residential Reentry and Home Confinement Services Located within the County Limits of Berkeley County, West Virginia.
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking providers for Residential Reentry Center (RRC) beds and Home Confinement services for male and female federal offenders in Berkeley County, West Virginia. Home Confinement placements must be within a 100?mile radius of the facility. Both RRC and Home Confinement services must follow the Federal Bureau of Prisons� Residential Reentry Center, March 2022 Statement of Work. Home Confinement requirements are defined in Chapter 10, with additional requirements noted throughout the SOW. This will be an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity type contract with firm fixed unit prices for all line items. The RRC requirement will consist of an estimated maximum of 40 beds in which 32 beds will be designated for males and 8 beds designated for females for the One-year Base Period and each of the Four One-year Option Periods The Home Confinement requirement will consist of an estimated maximum of 20 placements to include both males and females for the One-year Base Period and each of the Four One-year Option Periods. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC and HC) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. The Solicitation (RFP) will be available after October 10, 2026, exclusively on www.sam.gov. No hard copies will be provided. All updates will also be posted on this site, and interested parties are responsible for monitoring it for the latest information. The estimated closing date will be 60 days after the RFP is issued. All responsible sources may submit proposals. No collect calls will be accepted, and the agency will not accept telephone or written requests for the solicitation. Any questions regarding the pre-solicitation notice can be addressed to Rachel Brown at r16brown@bop.gov by 2:00PM MST on Friday, September 25, 2026.

title: D--Replacement of NWQL's Wastewater Treatment Monitor
description: Replacement of US Geological Survey (USGS), National Water Quality Laboratory's (NWQL) Wastewater Treatment Monitoring Computer System THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB). NO FORMAL SOLICITATION IS BEING REQUESTED UNDER THIS NOTICE. This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes to identify parties having an interest in and resources to support this requirement for replacement of wastewater SCADA computerized control system and software package using Inductive Automation or equivalent software that replicates the functionality of the current SCADA control system with modern, reliable hardware and software while minimizing operational downtime for the US Geological Survey (USGS), National Water Quality Laboratory (NWQL). The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The Government will review the information requested in this announcement based on the responses to this sources sought notice/market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses or procured through full and open competition. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services) and the size standard is $34.0 million. The following is a brief description of services that are required to be performed: A. Introduction: The US Geological Survey (USGS), National Water Quality Laboratory (NWQL) has a requirement for replacement of wastewater SCADA computerized control system and software package using Inductive Automation or equivalent software Inductive Automation or equivalent software that replicates the functionality of the current SCADA control system with modern, reliable hardware and software while minimizing operational downtime. B. Background: The USGS, NWQL operates a laboratory wastewater and treated ion exchange system. The Safety, Health, and Environmental (SHE) team relies on a computer-based supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) control system to assess discharge performance and maintain environmental compliance. The current system, installed in the mid 2000s, is aging and at risk of failure, which could result in operational shutdown of the laboratory. C. Scope of Work The Contractor shall provide all labor, software, programming, configuration, installation, testing, and documentation required to replace the existing wastewater SCADA control system. D. Technical Requirements: The Contractor shall provide the following: a. Installation, configuration and programming of Ignition Perspective HMI software b. Convert the existing Genesis32 software monitoring screens to Ignition Perspective and integrate logic, alarms and parameter settings. c. Integration of the Ignition Perspective software with the existing Allen Bradley PLC proprietary logic programing owned by others such that integration of the new software does not violate existing intellectual property ownership d. The new Ignition Perspective software will communicate with existing sensors, AB controllers, and treatment system components through the existing proprietary logic developed by others. e. System testing, commissioning, and acceptance verification f. Providing system documentation and operator training E. Functional Requirements: The new system shall: a. Seamless functionality with existing AB PLC proprietary logic programing own by others. b. Replicate and update current monitoring screens and functionality c. Interface with all existing sensors, PLCs, and control hardware d. Accurately measure, display, and record key wastewater parameters e. Provide alarm logic and notifications equivalent to the current system f. Automatically log discharge data for compliance records F. Installation Requirements: The Contractor shall: a. Coordinate installation to minimize downtime b. Ensure all work meets electrical and environmental safety standards c. Perform system cutover in a manner that maintains wastewater compliance capability (End of brief description of Services) If your organization has the potential ability to meet this requirement, please provide the following information to the Contracting Officer: 1. A tailored capability statement describing detailed information in providing wastewater SCADA computerized control system services outlined above. 2. The firm shall specify that they are either: 2.1 A small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, etc. and Or 2.2 Other than small business under the NAICS Code listed in the announcement. 2.3 The firm shall provide a point of contact name and e-mail information, and SAM.gov (Unique Entity ID (UEI) and must be registered and active in System for Award Management (SAM). All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary � the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Materials submitted to the Government for review will not be returned. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotations (RFQ) or Invitation for Bid (IFB). The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses received under this announcement. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated. In order to be responsive to this Notice, a firm shall provide the appropriate documentation for consideration by October 9, 2026 at 2:30 p.m. Mountain Daylight Time (MDT). Responses that do not comply with these procedures will not be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Inquiries will only be accepted by e-mail to Lisa Williams at lisa_williams@ios.doi.gov.

Cage _______ ref. no. ;09176 1780-1190; 3.2 Marking - This item shall be physically identified in accordance with ;MIL-STD-130, REV N, 16 NOV 2012; . 3.3 Changes in Design, Material Servicing, or Part Number - Except for a Code 1 change, which shall be processed as provided in the code statement shown below, no substitution of items shall be made until the NAVICP-MECH Contracting Officer has notified and approval has been given by issuance of a written change order. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. Roof top access may be required to place vertical antennas for UHF and VHF communications, Satellite Dish for Television Service, and open air HD Antenna for Standard Television Service. TSA administrative offices should not be located in windowed space that is adjacent to outside fire escapes, ledges or mezzanines. TSA administrative offices should be located in contiguous space on one floor, when available. Where possible, TSA administrative offices and support spaces should not be located on the top or ground levels of any building. In general, office spaces should be placed and glazed such that personnel cannot be seen from uncontrolled public areas. Preferably these offices should face courtyards, interior spaces or controlled areas. TSA offices should not be collocated in buildings or areas that handle, store, or ship Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT). TSA offices shall not be collocated in any facility where non-TSA personnel require daily access or emergency egress through TSA spaces. Offered space shall not be in the 100 year flood plain. title: Enterprise Air Route Surveillance Radar Replacement Sources Sought Request of Information
description: This is a Request for Information (RFI) in accordance with RFO 15.101(c). This RFI is issued to identify industry partners with capability to replace the current Air Route Surveillance Radar version 4 (ARSR-4) radars. The Government is planning the Air Route Surveillance Radar Replacement (ARSR-R) program to replace ARSR-4 systems across multiple fixed radar sites. The Government is seeking information from industry regarding capable, reliable, and sustainable radar solutions to support this long-term enterprise modernization.

title: BLU-138/B Penetrator Warhead
description: PURPOSE The U.S. Government (USG) is conducting market research to identify qualified sources for a potential BLU-138/B procurement. This effort will determine market competitiveness and assess the feasibility of a Small Business Set-Aside. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 332993 - Ammunition (except Small Arms) Manufacturing. This notice seeks industry feedback on capabilities, small business status, and preferred Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract lengths. Responses will validate acquisition strategy decisions. This is not a solicitation and does not guarantee a future contract. The Government encourages responses from all small businesses, including 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, HUBZone, and Women-Owned. Interested parties should provide: Confirmation of small business status under NAICS 332993 Description of anticipated teaming arrangements, specifying roles of the prime and partners. Summary of relevant experience delivering similar services to government or commercial customers within the past three years DESCRIPTION The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center Armament Directorate, Munitions Sustainment Division, GBU Components Branch (EBHC), Hill AFB, Utah seeks potential contractors with the technical expertise to produce: BLU-138/B 5000 lb. Advanced Penetrator Warhead (EMPTY CASE) CNU-754/E Shipping and Storage Container Taper Ring Taper Ring Set Screws Explosive fill is not part of this requirement. The BLU-138/B penetrator warhead is a 5000-pound class conventional penetrating weapon that fulfills the need for a capability to defeat specific very hard and deeply buried targets. Warhead assemblies must comply with the current Air Force BLU-138/B Technical Data Package (TDP). TDPs and specifications can be requested and will be provided via DoD SAFE to qualified respondents upon written request. Requests must include: Company name, mailing address, email, POC, phone number Current CAGE code and SAM.gov registration No reimbursement will be made for costs associated with providing information. Submission is voluntary and does not guarantee award. All responses to this Sources Sought must be submitted to the points of contact below. USG Points of Contact: Primary: Ryan Mitchell (ryan.mitchell.21@us.af.mil) Alternate: Nicholas Padgett (nicholas.padgett.2@us.af.mil) Any additional information will be posted on SAM.gov.

title: Air Vehicle Contractor Logistic Support
description: NOTE: Updated submission in below text now reflects a 9 Oct 26 date in line with the Genreal Information submission date. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational and market research purposes only in accordance with RFO (Revolutionary FAR Overhaul) Part 10. It does not constitute a solicitation, a Request for Proposal (RFP), or a promise to issue RFP in the future. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for expenses associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI. The information provided may be used by the U.S. Air Force in developing its acquisition strategy, Statement of Work (SOW), and performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition-sensitive information. BACKGROUND / DESCRIPTION The United States Air Force (USAF) operates a fleet of MH-139A aircraft for security and support missions. The aircraft is primarily used for security and transportation patrols across extensive intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) fields, while supporting search and rescue missions, and personnel/cargo transport. The aircraft platform is a commercial Leonardo AW139 helicopter modified by Boeing for military use. The existing fleet is twenty-six (26) aircraft with approximately thirty (30) additional aircraft planned in production. The fleet is disseminated at six (6) CONUS AFB locations. SCOPE OF REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) is seeking information from industry sources on the potential capability to provide Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) Services for the MH-139A (Grey Wolf) helicopter platform. The information provided by industry responders will be used to assess logistical support capability from contractors in the marketplace to assist the United States Government (USG) in refining its acquisition strategy as the MH-139A fleet transitions from its current Interim Contractor Support (ICS) and Interim Supply Support (ISS) postures to continued sustainment. The functional areas include, but are not limited to the list below:? Material Acquisitions Purchasing Management Support for Helicopter Rotable/Repairable Assets, Parts, and major Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) (e.g., engines, main gearboxes): Manage high-value components that can be physically repaired and reused rather than thrown away as well as disposable items that may or may not have a life limit. Purchasing Management Support for Consumable/Expendable Support: Manage a consumables program of parts as well as sourcing �one-time use� items required for daily maintenance. Purchasing Management Support for Test and Support Equipment: Procuring the specialized tools, stands, and calibration equipment necessary to test aircraft systems and to perform depot-level maintenance. Procurement Planning:?Execute timely, "just-in-time" procurement of scheduled maintenance materials to ensure parts are on hand prior to the commencement of heavy inspection events, minimizing aircraft downtime.? Inventory Management Inventory Stores Management: Operating the physical warehouse on base, tracking stock levels, and ensuring parts are ready for immediate issue to the flightline. Tool Crib Support Management: Manage and track check-in/check-out tooling usage for daily maintenance activity. Spares Management and APSR Integration: Maintain 100% floor-to-ceiling accountability of all Government Furnished Property (GFP) and spares using an approved DoD Accountable Property System of Record (APSR) (e.g., ELMS) that provides Total Asset Visibility (TAV) to the Government. Support Equipment (SE) Transition: Execute a 100% joint inventory, resolve discrepancies, and manage the physical relocation of all SE and tooling from incumbent facilities to operational bases, while maintaining strict calibration (AFMETCAL) and diagnostic software version control. FIAR and Accountability: Ensure strict adherence to Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) guidance by sustaining verifiable audit trails for all asset lifecycle transactions, enabling accurate financial valuation, and supporting independent audits to guarantee total operational accountability." Maintenance Management Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Depot Flow Plan (DFP): Develop, maintain, and execute a comprehensive Depot Flow Plan (DFP) detailing aircraft retrofit and modification schedules to be coordinated with the SPO. Over and Above (O&A) Management: Possess a structured process to identify, document, estimate, and execute O&A repairs for unprogrammed work (e.g., severe corrosion or structural defects) discovered during inspections. Analytical Condition Inspections (ACI): Integrate structured ACI activities into planned depot work to foreclose structural integrity risks. Depot component Level Maintenance Management Scheduled / Time Inspection Events Maintainers must proactively execute TCTOs and engineering directives. Maintainers must also submit, respond to, and resolve technical requests, coordinating directly with Field Service Representatives and OEM engineers as required. Scheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Modifications, Technical Order/Engineering Order event activity: Physically installing hardware/software upgrades or safety modifications on the aircraft flightline Depot-level repair actions must comply with directed TCTOs and engineering dispositions. Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Reliability and Engineering Data Analysis: The contractor shall establish a robust data analytics program to provide the Government with full transparency into component lifecycle health. This includes conducting continuous Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) and providing detailed maintenance shop data. The contractor must generate and report true Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM) metrics (e.g., Mean Time Between Failure [MTBF], Mean Time To Repair [MTTR]) for both the airframe and individual components Component Depot Level Maintenance Activity Repair Order Management � Outsourcing Service Orders Component Warranty Management Component Modifications Programs Airworthiness Directives, TCTOs, Service Bulletins, Service Information Letters: Monitoring and implementing FAA, OEM, or military airworthiness alerts to ensure the aircraft remains legally certified to fly. Contract Field Team Provide CFTs for tasks requiring shop facilities, tooling, support equipment, processes beyond organizational level capability technical manuals, and/or personnel of higher technical skills. Field Team Logistics: For all CFT deployments, the contractor shall be solely responsible for coordinating all personnel requirements, scheduling work, obtaining workspace, securing base access/clearances, and provisioning all required tools and Support Equipment. Engineering Support OEM Engineering Reach-Back and Data Currency: The contractor shall establish and maintain a direct line of communication and authorized data exchange with the Type Certificate (TC) holder (Leonardo). Technical Order and Engineering Order Management STC Management Deficiency Report Analysis and Investigation Health and Usage Monitoring Systems (HUMS): The contractor shall utilize aircraft diagnostic data (e.g., from HUMS/HELIWISE systems) to actively review fleet health, predict component degradation, and recommend proactive or unscheduled maintenance prior to catastrophic failure. Reliability and Maintainability Management Program (RAMMP): Manage a formal RAMMP in accordance with the Life Cycle Sustainment Plan (LCSP) to address, track, and correct R&M problems. description: SYNOPSIS The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), C3BM?Directorate,?Wright Patterson?Force Base (WPAFB),?Ohio?is conducting market research seeking vendor interest for?a?Ground-Based, Medium-Caliber Gun Weapon System. ?
