Additionally, Non-Government A&AS support may be?utilized?in the review process of RFI submissions. These non-governmental support staff are covered directly by Nondisclosure Agreements (NDAs) with the US Government as a condition of employment. Any respondent to the RFI with concern should notify one of the POCs found in Section 7.?? PURPOSE The Government is conducting market research to identify potential industry sources capable of providing solutions for a Ground-Based, Medium-Caliber Gun Weapon System that fires affordable munitions, enables defense against air and missile threats with an initial focus on subsonic cruise missiles (CM) and Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) to provide persistent defense in support of United States Air Force assets. The objective of this RFI is to gather information regarding industry capability. ACQUISITION STRATEGY? The program's acquisition strategy is currently in development.? SCOPE/REQUIREMENTS The scope of this RFI is centered on solutions that strictly prioritize fifteen baseline attributes essential to operational success that can engage both cruise missiles and UAS (groups 1-5) threats in accordance with the reference documents. To effectively assess and compare air defense weapon system performance, there are fifteen critical baseline operational and technical parameters that must be analyzed in unison. These key metrics begin with the system's Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) evaluated against both Cruise Missiles (CM) and Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Groups 1-5 at maximum range and altitude, ensuring robust lethality against diverse modern threats. The physical footprint of the engagement envelope is defined by its Effective Slant Range and Elevation Coverage, while the capacity for sustained operations is dictated by Magazine Depth and the system's ability to execute Raid Handling against saturating attacks. Furthermore, modern multi-domain operations require seamless Integrated Sensor Capability, deep C2 System Integration, and broad System Interoperability across joint networks. From an efficiency and sustainment standpoint, the system must balance its Cost Per Engagement and Manpower requirements, supported by a reliable Built-in-Test (BIT) framework for rapid diagnostics. Finally, tactical utility is rounded out by the platform's overall Transportability, stringent Weapon Safety protocols, and its comprehensive Multi-Domain Engagement Capability to counter threats across various operational environments. Fifteen Baseline Requirements: Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) vs CM at max range and altitude Salvo Probability of Kill (Pk) vs UAS Groups 1-5 at max range and altitude Effective Slant Range Elevation Coverage Magazine Depth Raid Handling Integrated Sensor Capability C2 System Integration System Interoperability Cost Per Engagement Manpower Built-in-Test (BIT) Transportability Weapon Safety Multi-Domain Engagement Capability When designing and evaluating next-generation defense systems, the development team must navigate critical trade-offs across three primary Trade Space Attributes to balance lethality, situational awareness, and operational flexibility. First, the system must optimize Munition Performance versus Munition Cost and Gun Capability, ensuring that the interceptor's velocity, maneuverability, and terminal effects are maximized without driving the cost-per-engagement to unsustainable levels or exceeding the physical constraints of the host platform. Second, developers must carefully select the Organic Sensor Capability and Phenomenology�integrating the right mix of radar, electro-optical, infrared, or radio-frequency sensors�to ensure reliable target acquisition and tracking across varying weather conditions, environments, and countermeasure scenarios. Finally, the entire architecture must remain Rapidly Deployable, maintaining a lightweight, modular, and transportable footprint that can be swiftly projected into austere theater environments to meet emergent threats. The final NAICS determination will depend on the final acquisition strategy and selected contract vehicle. title: ECP 6315C3 Navigation Warfare NAVWAR A-Kits for F/A-18E/F Aircraft
description: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of the F/A-18 and EA-18G Program Office (PMA-265), is issuing this Sources Sought Notice as a market research tool to identify potential parties having an interest, knowledge and resources required to support manufacturing, assembly and installation of Engineering Change Proposal (ECP) 6315C3 A-Kits Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR) ECP 6315C3. The NAVWAR A-Kits support aircraft integration for both United States Navy (USN) and Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) F/A-18 and EA-18G configurations. This effort encompasses engineering and manufacturing tasks include, but are not limited to: Manufacturing assembly planning and execution. Structural sheet metal fabrication, machining, and finishing. Electrical wiring harness and RF cabling assembly. Program reporting and quality control documentation. The contractor shall be responsible for obtaining from The Boeing Company all aircraft data, manufacturing specifications, and proprietary specification data necessary to manufacture and install the A-Kits. The Boeing Company is the only known source that possesses requisite technical data, unique and specialized engineering capability, subject matter expertise, resources, tooling, facilities, and manufacturing processes used on the F/A-18 and EA-18G aircraft platforms. DISCLAIMER:?THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), BUT RATHER A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) from industry that will allow the Government to identify interested sources capable of meeting the requirements. This RFI is issued solely for market research, planning and information purposes and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to enter into a contractual agreement, nor will the Government pay for information solicited hereunder. Technical Data Strategy Clear, documented evidence of existing access in obtaining technical data, designs, and specifications for the F/A-18 and EA-18G aircraft. Manufacturing Experience A detailed description of Company's experience in procuring and qualifying obsolete electronic aviation components within military aerospace applications. Quality Assurance & Certifications A description of the company's quality management system, including relevant industry certifications and specialized process qualifications. Commerciality and Lead Times Information regarding available vendor commercial price lists for related items, current stock levels, and typical production lead times Any other relevant information that demonstrates the company's ability to meet the Government's requirements. Responses shall be submitted electronically to the designated Contract Specialist, Cassaundra Somerville, in Microsoft Word format or Portable Document Format (PDF) at the following email address: cassaundra.e.somerville.civ@us.navy.mil (or DOD Safe for larger files). All responses, including capability statements, shall be submitted no later than 5:00 PM EST, 09 October 2026. All information submitted should be unclassified. Questions or comments regarding this notice may be addressed to Procuring Contracting Officer, Mr. Ryan Bodine and Contract Specialist, Cassaundra Somerville.

description: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational and market research purposes only in accordance with RFO (Revolutionary FAR Overhaul) Part 10. It does not constitute a solicitation, a Request for Proposal (RFP), or a promise to issue RFP in the future. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition-sensitive information. BACKGROUND / DESCRIPTION The United States Air Force (USAF) operates a fleet of MH-139A aircraft for security and support missions. The aircraft is primarily used for security and transportation patrols across extensive intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) fields, while supporting search and rescue missions, and personnel/cargo transport. The aircraft platform is a commercial Leonardo AW139 helicopter modified by Boeing for military use. The existing fleet is twenty-six (26) aircraft with approximately thirty (30) additional aircraft planned in production. The fleet is disseminated at six (6) CONUS AFB locations. SCOPE OF REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) is seeking information from industry sources on the potential capability to provide Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) Services for the MH-139A (Grey Wolf) helicopter platform. The information provided by industry responders will be used to assess logistical support capability from contractors in the marketplace to assist the United States Government (USG) in refining its acquisition strategy as the MH-139A fleet transitions from its current Interim Contractor Support (ICS) and Interim Supply Support (ISS) postures to continued sustainment. The functional areas include, but are not limited to the list below:? Material Acquisitions Purchasing Management Support for Helicopter Rotable/Repairable Assets, Parts, and major Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) (e.g., engines, main gearboxes): Manage high-value components that can be physically repaired and reused rather than thrown away as well as disposable items that may or may not have a life limit. Purchasing Management Support for Consumable/Expendable Support: Manage a consumables program of parts as well as sourcing �one-time use� items required for daily maintenance. Purchasing Management Support for Test and Support Equipment: Procuring the specialized tools, stands, and calibration equipment necessary to test aircraft systems and to perform depot-level maintenance. Procurement Planning:?Execute timely, "just-in-time" procurement of scheduled maintenance materials to ensure parts are on hand prior to the commencement of heavy inspection events, minimizing aircraft downtime.? Inventory Management Inventory Stores Management: Operating the physical warehouse on base, tracking stock levels, and ensuring parts are ready for immediate issue to the flightline. Tool Crib Support Management: Manage and track check-in/check-out tooling usage for daily maintenance activity. Spares Management and APSR Integration: Maintain 100% floor-to-ceiling accountability of all Government Furnished Property (GFP) and spares using an approved DoD Accountable Property System of Record (APSR) (e.g., ELMS) that provides Total Asset Visibility (TAV) to the Government. Support Equipment (SE) Transition: Execute a 100% joint inventory, resolve discrepancies, and manage the physical relocation of all SE and tooling from incumbent facilities to operational bases, while maintaining strict calibration (AFMETCAL) and diagnostic software version control. FIAR and Accountability: Ensure strict adherence to Financial Improvement and Audit Readiness (FIAR) guidance by sustaining verifiable audit trails for all asset lifecycle transactions, enabling accurate financial valuation, and supporting independent audits to guarantee total operational accountability." Maintenance Management Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Depot Flow Plan (DFP): Develop, maintain, and execute a comprehensive Depot Flow Plan (DFP) detailing aircraft retrofit and modification schedules to be coordinated with the SPO. Over and Above (O&A) Management: Possess a structured process to identify, document, estimate, and execute O&A repairs for unprogrammed work (e.g., severe corrosion or structural defects) discovered during inspections. Analytical Condition Inspections (ACI): Integrate structured ACI activities into planned depot work to foreclose structural integrity risks. Depot component Level Maintenance Management Scheduled / Time Inspection Events Maintainers must proactively execute TCTOs and engineering directives. Maintainers must also submit, respond to, and resolve technical requests, coordinating directly with Field Service Representatives and OEM engineers as required. Scheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Modifications, Technical Order/Engineering Order event activity: Physically installing hardware/software upgrades or safety modifications on the aircraft flightline Depot-level repair actions must comply with directed TCTOs and engineering dispositions. Heavy (Depot Level) Maintenance Management Unscheduled / Time Inspection Events Unscheduled Hourly Inspection Events: Inspections triggered strictly by aircraft flight hours Reliability and Engineering Data Analysis: The contractor shall establish a robust data analytics program to provide the Government with full transparency into component lifecycle health. This includes conducting continuous Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analysis (FMECA) and providing detailed maintenance shop data. The contractor must generate and report true Reliability, Availability, and Maintainability (RAM) metrics (e.g., Mean Time Between Failure [MTBF], Mean Time To Repair [MTTR]) for both the airframe and individual components Component Depot Level Maintenance Activity Repair Order Management � Outsourcing Service Orders Component Warranty Management Component Modifications Programs Airworthiness Directives, TCTOs, Service Bulletins, Service Information Letters: Monitoring and implementing FAA, OEM, or military airworthiness alerts to ensure the aircraft remains legally certified to fly. Contract Field Team Provide CFTs for tasks requiring shop facilities, tooling, support equipment, processes beyond organizational level capability technical manuals, and/or personnel of higher technical skills. Field Team Logistics: For all CFT deployments, the contractor shall be solely responsible for coordinating all personnel requirements, scheduling work, obtaining workspace, securing base access/clearances, and provisioning all required tools and Support Equipment. Engineering Support OEM Engineering Reach-Back and Data Currency: The contractor shall establish and maintain a direct line of communication and authorized data exchange with the Type Certificate (TC) holder (Leonardo). Technical Order and Engineering Order Management STC Management Deficiency Report Analysis and Investigation Health and Usage Monitoring Systems (HUMS): The contractor shall utilize aircraft diagnostic data (e.g., from HUMS/HELIWISE systems) to actively review fleet health, predict component degradation, and recommend proactive or unscheduled maintenance prior to catastrophic failure. Reliability and Maintainability Management Program (RAMMP): Manage a formal RAMMP in accordance with the Life Cycle Sustainment Plan (LCSP) to address, track, and correct R&M problems. Responses to this Sources Sought must be received by email no later than the date specified in the response section. This intent of this sources sought is for market research to make appropriate acquisition decisions and to gain knowledge of potential qualified Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses, 8(a), HUBZone, and other Small Businesses interested and capable of performing the proposed contract work. Documentation of technical expertise must be presented in sufficient detail for the Government to determine that your company has the capability and experience to compete for this acquisition. title: C--Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA) and Defense Nuclear Weapons School (DNWS
description: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA) and Defense Nuclear Weapons School (DNWS) are seeking experienced architecture and engineering services to modernize the Nuclear Weapons Instructional Museum (NWIM) at Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico. The facility serves as a classified museum preserving the history and development of the U.S. nuclear weapons stockpile and is used as a key instructional and training resource. See attached Sources Sought Notice and Draft Statement of Work.

title: Denmark – Construction work – Faciliteter til Hærens Tunge Brigade (FHTB) på 582 Aalborg Kaserne - Bygningsnummer 157 og 158 samt etablering af parkering.
description: Nærværende projekt er en del af Forsvarskommandoens og ETK's samlede plan for "Faciliteter til Hærens Tunge Brigade" (FHTB) FHTB omfatter ombygning og nybygning på en række etablissementer rundt i landet, som skal sikre faciliteterne til Hærens Tunge Brigade. Nærværende udbud vedrører hovedentreprisen på 582 Aalborg Kaserne. Byggeriet på Aalborg Kaserne omfatter følgende: Projektet omfatter opførelse af to identiske garagebygninger med tilhørende kontortårne. Hver bygning består af en central garagefacilitet til understøttelse af den daglige drift samt to integrerede kontortårne i tre etager placeret i bygningens ender. Kontortårnene indeholder arbejdspladser, møde- og undervisningsfaciliteter samt de nødvendige velfærdsfunktioner, herunder opholdsrum, omklædning og øvrige personalefaciliteter. Garagebygningerne indrettes til køretøjer, materiel og tilhørende driftsfunktioner, mens kontortårnene samler de administrative funktioner og skaber moderne rammer for både ledelse, planlægning og personale. Bygningernes udformning sikrer en funktionel sammenhæng mellem drifts- og kontorfunktioner samt gode interne forbindelser mellem arbejdsområderne. Projektet omfatter også manøvre- og kørselsarealer omkring bygningerne, som sikrer adgang og effektiv drift for større køretøjer. Derudover etableres P Syd, en større parkeringsplads til lastbiler og andre tunge køretøjer. Området indrettes med fokus på trafiksikkerhed og funktionalitet, herunder tydelig adskillelse af kørende og gående trafik samt sikre gangforbindelser mellem parkeringsarealerne, bygningerne og områdets øvrige funktioner. Hovedmængder Det samlede bruttoareal pr. bygning udgør ca. 6.563 m2 fordelt på: 1. etage: ca. 3.686 m2 2. etage: ca. 1.866 m2 3. etage: ca. 1.011 m2 Samlet bygningsareal (2 x 6.563 m2) = 13.126 m2 Terræn ved bygning 157 og 158 • Ca. 29.000 m2 coloc-belægning omkring bygninger og tilhørende manøvrearealer. • Parkeringsfaciliteter til ca. 100 personbiler. P Syd • Ca. 45.000 m2 coloc-belægning. • Ca. 3.000 m2 grønne arealer med beplantning. • Ca. 1.000 m2 gangarealer. • Ovenstående skal indeholde ca. 295 parkeringspladser til tunge køretøjer (12,5 x 5,8 m), hvoraf en væsentlig del er disponeret med mulighed for parkering af køretøjer op til 25 m længde. For så vidt angår det nærmere indhold af hovedentreprisen henvises til det øvrige udbudsmateriale, som af sikkerhedsmæssige årsager først udleveres på det tidspunkt, hvor de virksomheder, som ETK prækvalificerer til at afgive tilbud, har underskrevet en fortrolighedserklæring, jf. pkt. 3. Ansøgers anmodning om prækvalifikation skal således alene afgives på baggrund af oplysningerne i nærværende prækvalifikationsbetingelser.

title: Ingenieurleistungen nach Teil 4 Abschnitt 2 HOAI
description: 88239 Wangen, Lindauer Str. 28, WG,AG,Lindauer28,(S),Sanier+Erweiterbau, Ingenieurleistungen nach Teil 4 Abschnitt 2 HOAI. Beabsichtigt ist die stufenweise Beauftragung von Fachplanungsleistungen nach Teil 4 Abschnitt 2 HOAI. In Verbindung mit diesem Verfahren sollen die Grundleistungen der Leistungsphasen 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 und 8, sowie besondere Leistungen der Leistungsphasen 3, 5 und 8 vergeben werden. Planung eines Neubaus/Anbaus mit den kompletten Installationen für die KG 410, KG 420, KG 430 und KG 480. Ertüchtigung des Bestandsgebäudes mit Anpassungsarbeiten für den Zusammenschluss mit dem Neubau im Bereich der Wärmeversorgung. Für die Bauaufgabe ist eine Kostenvorgabe in Höhe von rd. 405.000€ brutto (KG 410 +KG 420 +KG 430 +KG 480) vorgesehen. Die Bauplanung ist ab 11/2026, die Baudurchführung von 09/2028 bis 09/2031 vorgesehen.
